name: Hara Saabha Vimochana Perumal Temple, Thirukkandiyur
deity: Vishnu as Hara Saabha Vimochana Perumal, standing, with the Goddess Kamalavalli Nachiyar — the lord who freed Shiva from a curse
period: A Divya Desam of the Chola country, sung by Thirumangai Alvar in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham
dynasty: Chola, with later Vijayanagara and Nayak additions
summary: At Thirukkandiyur near Thiruvaiyaru, Vishnu stands as Hara Saabha Vimochana Perumal, who released Shiva from the curse of Brahma's skull — a Chola-country Divya Desam sung by Thirumangai Alvar.

sections.history: Thirukkandiyur, in the Thanjavur district near Thiruvaiyaru, is one of the 108 Divya Desams in Chola Nadu, the abodes of Vishnu sung by the Alvars in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham. Thirumangai Alvar honours the Lord here in a single pasuram. The temple is attributed to the medieval Cholas, around the later eighth century, and received additions under the Vijayanagara rulers and the Madurai Nayaks. It is remembered as a Trimurti kshetram, and tradition holds that the Lord appeared visibly to the sage Agastya here. Close by, a few hundred metres away, stands the Shiva temple of Brahmasirakandeeswarar, so that the two great traditions share the village.
sections.architecture: The sanctum stands under the Kamalakruthi Vimanam, the lotus-shaped vimana, and Hara Saabha Vimochana Perumal stands facing east. His consort, Kamalavalli Nachiyar, has her own shrine. The temple tank is the Kapala Moksha Pushkarini, also called the Kamala Theertham, whose name recalls the legend of the skull. The temple follows the Dravidian manner of the Chola country, with later Vijayanagara and Nayak work in its halls and enclosures.
sections.legends: The sthala purana tells that Shiva once severed one of Brahma's five heads, and the skull clung to his hand as a curse that no pilgrimage could remove. Coming to Thirukkandiyur, he worshipped Vishnu and the Goddess Kamalavalli, and the skull fell away from his hand. The Lord is therefore called Hara Saabha Vimochana, the one who released Hara from the curse, and the tank is the Kapala Moksha Pushkarini, the tank of the skull's release. The nearby Shiva temple remembers the same story from the other side.
sections.festivals: The temple keeps the Brahmotsavam in the month of Panguni, March–April, and the Pavitrotsavam in Aippasi. Vaikunta Ekadashi and the lamp festival of Karthigai Deepam are also observed. Processions and special worship mark these days. Confirm dates locally, as they follow the Tamil almanac.
sections.experience: A quiet village Divya Desam where the pilgrim can walk between a Vishnu temple and a Shiva temple that share one legend. Pause at the Kapala Moksha Pushkarini and look up at the lotus-shaped vimana. It fits easily into a day among the temples of Thiruvaiyaru and Thanjavur.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening darshan sessions and a midday closure; Vaikunta Ekadashi is the busiest day. Confirm current timings before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: Thirukkandiyur lies near Thiruvaiyaru, on the road between Thanjavur and Thiruvaiyaru in Thanjavur district. Thanjavur Junction is the nearest major railway station, and Tiruchirappalli International Airport the nearest airport; buses and taxis serve the last stretch by road.
